edits.old:
Several further identifications remain questions. Does positivity characterize bigness, at least for nef backgrounds on an arbitrary compact complex manifold? The preceding section identifies the extrema over smooth densities on the positive cone. What further comparison is valid for volumes attached to singular classes? What modification law is valid when the pullback of a smooth positive probability measure vanishes on the exceptional divisor? The present proof uses strict positivity of the density for its smooth equation and its minimizing metric. It does not establish a birational transformation law for degenerate pulled-back densities, nor an intersection volume for an arbitrary b-divisor family.

For a finite divisor on $X$, the residual construction and its exact feasibility threshold are now available. Extending them to compatible residual classes on all modifications, or identifying them with normalizations in general prescribed envelope classes, still requires further theorems. The explicit failure of envelope-system recovery shows why taking a perturbation limit and then discarding its extra divisorial singularities cannot be assumed to preserve such a theory.
edits.new: For fixed finite divisor support, \cref{prop:finite-divisorial-equation-limits} gives exact limiting singularities while the residual backgrounds remain positive. General compatible classes involve an additional difficulty: the pullback of $\mu$ may vanish on the exceptional divisor. Neither the smooth equation nor its minimizing metric applies to that density without further estimates. The example in \cref{sec:envelope-boundary-example} shows that prescribed ideal type can also be lost in a perturbation limit.

edits.old: One possible intermediate target is a finite collection of divisorial constraints with residual backgrounds in a compact subset of the positive cone. The explicit finite-divisor equations can then test whether the limiting ideal coefficients remain exact. Extending such a statement to infinitely many models requires new uniform estimates; finite-level compatibility alone does not supply them.
edits.new: For fixed finite divisor support, \cref{prop:finite-divisorial-equation-limits} gives a positive-cone case: if the coefficients converge and the limiting residual background still has a smooth positive representative, the normalized smooth remainders converge smoothly. The singular equation solutions converge in capacity, their measures converge in total variation, and their logarithmic coefficients remain exact on every modification. Multiplier ideals can nevertheless jump at an integer coefficient. This concerns the canonical equation family on one manifold; recovery of a general envelope system and estimates uniform over infinitely many models still require additional arguments.

edits.old: The general-measure existence constructions in the two stated regimes are now complete, including the ordinary-type $L^p$ conclusion. Further equation work should address the remaining hypotheses, regularity and singular-space descent. The minimal $L^p$ construction uses the invariant Gauduchon trace in \cref{prop:big-singular-gauduchon-trace}; the arbitrary-model estimate uses relative moments and contact envelopes. Neither replaces individual masses by a cohomological constant. The bounded estimates already give H\"older continuity in a Hermitian background and local continuity in a semipositive big background wherever a fixed strict barrier is locally bounded; see \cref{thm:local-big-bounded-continuity}. Those regularity statements use no bounded mass hypothesis.
edits.new: Further equation work should address positive individual thresholds without positive lower mass, and descent through singular spaces. The proved general-measure results retain their two distinct geometric regimes. For bounded solutions, \cref{thm:local-big-bounded-continuity} gives local continuity wherever a fixed strict barrier is locally bounded, without a bounded mass hypothesis.

Each calculation has an exact successful model in the book and an explicit obstruction showing what cannot be omitted.

\subsection{Varying divisorial coefficients}

For fixed divisor support, the residual equation also controls limits while its background stays in the positive cone. Fix distinct prime divisors $D_1,\ldots,D_N$, their metrics and logarithmic potentials $\sigma_j=\log|s_j|^2$, a smooth real background $\theta$, and a smooth strictly positive probability measure $\mu$. For $a\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^N$ put
\[
 D_a=\sum_j a_jD_j,\qquad
 \sigma_a=\sum_{a_j>0}a_j\sigma_j,\qquad
 \beta_a=\theta-\sum_j a_j\eta_j.
\]
Write $\mathcal A$ for the set of such $a$ for which $\beta_a$ has a smooth positive representative. Zero coefficients are omitted from the logarithmic sum.

\Needspace{28\baselineskip}
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:finite-divisorial-equation-limits}
There are uniquely normalized smooth functions $v_a$, $a\in\mathcal A$, such that
\[
 \int_Xv_a\,\mathrm{d}\mu=0,\qquad
 \Omega_a=\beta_a+\ddc v_a>0,\qquad
 \Omega_a^n=c(a)\mu,
 \quad c(a)=\mathcal V_\mu(\beta_a)>0.
\]
The maps $a\mapsto v_a$ and $a\mapsto c(a)$ are smooth, with bounds for every smooth norm of $v_a$ on compact subsets of $\mathcal A$. Here smoothness at a zero coefficient means restriction of a smooth family from an open neighborhood in $\mathbb R^N$.

Set $u_a=\sigma_a+v_a$. If $a^{(k)}\in\mathcal A$ and $a^{(k)}\to a\in\mathcal A$, then $u_{a^{(k)}}\to u_a$ in $L^1$ and in capacity, and smoothly on compact subsets of $X\setminus\bigcup_jD_j$. Moreover,
\[
 \bigl\|\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_\theta(u_{a^{(k)}})
       -\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_\theta(u_a)\bigr\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
       =|c(a^{(k)})-c(a)|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every modification $\pi:Y\to X$ with smooth source and every prime divisor $E\subset Y$,
\[
 \nu(u_a\circ\pi,E)=\sum_j a_j\operatorname{ord}_E(\pi^*D_j).
\]
In particular the limit has exactly the prescribed divisorial ordinary type; no additional singularity occurs in this finite family.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The set of parameters in $\mathbb R^N$ for which $\beta_a$ has a smooth positive representative is open. The smooth equation gives $v_a$ and $c(a)$ there. With the fixed mean normalization, the implicit-function argument in \cref{prop:gaud-volume-first-variation} gives their smooth dependence on this finite-dimensional family. Smooth uniqueness makes the local solution families agree. A finite covering of any compact parameter set then gives all the asserted smooth bounds.

The Poincar\'e--Lelong identity gives
\[
 \theta+\ddc u_a=[D_a]+\Omega_a.
\]
Thus $u_a\in\PSH(X,\theta)$. Its extended measure equals $\Omega_a^n=c(a)\mu$ off the divisor union, and both measures vanish on that union. This also treats $D_a=0$. Each fixed $\sigma_j$ is locally integrable, so coefficient convergence and smooth convergence of $v_a$ give the $L^1$ limit. Off the fixed divisor union every $\sigma_j$ is smooth, which gives the asserted smooth convergence. For capacity convergence, remove an open neighborhood of that analytic set of arbitrarily small Hermitian capacity. On its compact complement the convergence is uniform. This proves capacity convergence, since the divisor union has capacity zero. The equality of total-variation distances follows from the equation and $\mu(X)=1$.

Finally, after pullback the logarithmic potential $\sigma_j\circ\pi$ has generic coefficient $\operatorname{ord}_E(\pi^*D_j)$, whereas $v_a\circ\pi$ is smooth. Additivity for the finite logarithmic sum proves the displayed formula on every model. Since $v_a$ is smooth also at the limiting parameter, $u_a$ has the ordinary type of $\sigma_a$.
\end{proof}

The positive-cone hypothesis is imposed at the limit as well as along the sequence. The statement concerns equation solutions with finitely many prescribed divisors on a fixed manifold. It does not prove recovery for arbitrary envelope systems or supply estimates uniform over all modifications.

Multiplier ideals need not be eventually constant in this family. At a smooth point of $D_j$ outside the other divisors, take a coordinate $z_1$ defining $D_j$. There $u_a=a_j\log|z_1|^2+O(1)$, so
\[
 \mathcal I(u_a)=(z_1^{\lfloor a_j\rfloor})
\]
by the one-variable integral in \cref{ex:ideal-disc} and Fubini's theorem. Thus, if the parameter stays in $\mathcal A$ while $a_j$ increases to an integer from below, this local ideal jumps at the limit. Exactness of the limiting logarithmic coefficients does not mean eventual equality of the multiplier ideals.

edits.old: We justify replacing bounded potentials by smooth strictly positive ones in the extrema defining $v_\pm$. If $u\in\PSH(X,\omega)\cap L^\infty$, \cref{thm:bounded-exact-regularization} gives smooth $\omega$-plurisubharmonic $u_j$ decreasing to $u$. Their bounded Monge--Amp\`ere measures converge by monotone continuity, including their total masses on compact $X$. For fixed $j$, the potentials $(1-\delta)u_j$, $0<\delta<1$, are strictly positive in background $\omega$, and their masses tend to that of $u_j$ as $\delta\downarrow0$, by the smooth polynomial expansion. Every bounded mass is therefore a limit of strictly positive smooth masses. The reverse inclusion is immediate. This proves the first two identities, without a uniform bound on those masses.
